checked: Checked the equally likely probability model, complement rule, multiplication and addition rules, independence and dependence claims, probability bounds, and gambler's-fallacy statement; each is mathematically correct.
Checked the standard-deck facts: 52 cards, four 13-card suits, 26 red and 26 black cards, 12 face cards, and four cards of each rank are correct.
Example 1 solved independently: outcomes greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.
Example 2 solved independently: six of the 36 ordered two-die outcomes sum to 7, so the probability is 6/36 = 1/6.
Example 3 solved independently: head and 6 has probability (1/2)(1/6) = 1/12.
Example 4 solved independently: two reds without replacement has probability (5/8)(4/7) = 20/56 = 5/14.
Example 5 solved independently: king or queen is 8/52 = 2/13; king or heart is (4 + 13 - 1)/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.
Example 6 solved independently: at least one head in three tosses is 1 - (1/2)^3 = 7/8.
